transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Liu (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (BrightScale CTO), Marcus Lee (BrightScale ML Eng), Dana Ortiz (BrightScale Platform)

Auto-summary: quick product walkthrough of Redwood API and Console, focused on migrating existing OpenAI/Anthropic/Together integrations. Customer wants to validate parity and run small pilot.

00:00 Jordan Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jordan from redwood, uh sofia our se will walk through the migration parity mapping and demo. how's everyone's day?
00:08 Aisha Khan: good, thanks, excited to see how this maps to our openai stack, we run a mix of openai and anthropic and a bunch of together models for internal and customer-facing agents.
00:18 Jordan Park: perfect, quick run of agenda: parity table, API/SDK examples, console/optimize features for batching and caching, security and private deployment notes, then next steps. sofia?
00:28 Sofia Liu: yeah i'll jump in on the demo, i'll show the api surface first, then a quick console tour for routing and optimize suggestions. note: i'll call out differences when we see them, sometimes names are slightly different like 'createCompletion' vs 'generate' - we try to keep one-to-one mapping but there are small param differences.
00:45 Marcus Lee: quick question before you start - streaming and function calling are critical for us, we use function calling heavily in production.
00:53 Sofia Liu: totally - we have streaming with delta events and a function-calling contract similar to openai. i'll demo a sample call in a sec.
01:02 Sofia Liu: (screen share) ok here's the redwood request example, you see endpoint /v1/generate, body fields: model, input, max_tokens, temperature, and we also support messages for chat-style models. For function-calling we use a schema block; the handler returns structured json and we provide tooling for validation.
01:28 Dana Ortiz: is there an official sdk mapping? we have a small node/python library that wraps openai calls, we want minimal code change.
01:36 Jordan Park: yes, we provide SDK shims and code snippets for node/python/go - basically 1-2 lines change in many cases. we'll share a parity mapping doc that lists parameter equivalences.
01:50 Sofia Liu: here's an example streaming response, you can see partial tokens come as events. small note: in some open-source backends tokenization differs so you may see slight delta in token counts but end-to-end behavior is consistent.
02:10 Marcus Lee: cost question - how do tokens convert? we pay per token with openai, does redwood do per-token as well?
02:18 Jordan Park: for hosted the pricing is per-token and per-embedding unit similar-ish. for dedicated you commit capacity and get a different unit economics. we'll provide a sample calc comparing your current monthly to projected redwood hosted vs dedicated.
02:34 Aisha Khan: our bigger concern is latency and tail p99; for customer agents we're seeing p99 spikes that matter. can redwood match that?
02:42 Sofia Liu: yes, we focus on latency SLOs, we support autoscaling and dedicated pools for predictable p99; also batching/kv prefix cache reduces downstream work. if you want we can run a p99-focused perf test with your representative payloads.
03:00 Marcus Lee: that would be great. we'll provide the payloads.
03:05 Sofia Liu: perfect. moving on to embeddings - we support standard embedding endpoints, you can swap in calls with minimal changes, similarity search and reranking are supported in the console, and optimize can recommend quantization or batching profiles for embeddings-heavy workloads.
03:28 Dana Ortiz: any differences around embeddings dimensionality? we use 1536 dims for one of our models.
03:35 Sofia Liu: we map to model-specific dims; if you pick a particular open model we document dims. in the parity sheet we'll include dims and quantization notes.
03:46 Jordan Park: security - briefly, we offer hosted with SOC2, and private options: VPC control plane and on-prem. we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management and provide audit logs.
03:59 Aisha Khan: do you have SSO/SAML and RBAC for console access? we need strict least-privilege.
04:06 Jordan Park: yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC and RBAC in the console, and we can restrict routes and models per team. we'll send the security pack.
04:18 Marcus Lee: any encryption at rest caveats for dedicated?
04:22 Sofia Liu: dedicated supports customer-managed encryption keys via KMS; for on-prem obviously you control everything. we'll have our infra doc attached.
04:33 Dana Ortiz: networking - does private mean VPC peering or a private agent in our VPC?
04:38 Jordan Park: both options exist. VPC peering for control plane with private endpoints, or fully private deployment that runs in your environment. we'll have a follow-up scoping call for network diagrams.
04:52 Sofia Liu: demo: console route config - you can create a route, pin a model version, choose fallback variants (e.g., quantized cheaper model) and set traffic split for canary. this is useful when migrating - you can start with a small percentage of traffic to redwood and fall back to openai if latency or errors spike.
05:14 Aisha Khan: can we do A/B for different model families? we want to compare anthopic and openai variants.
05:20 Sofia Liu: yes you can configure model variants and do rollouts, redwood supports multi-model routing by policy.
05:27 Marcus Lee: about function calling when you fallback to openai, how do you maintain deterministic behavior?
05:34 Sofia Liu: function calling contract should be identical, but you'll need to ensure schema compatibility; the parity sheet will highlight edge cases - for example some models return different structure for stop sequences or streaming chunk boundaries.
05:50 Jordan Park: okay time to show a short migration example - swapping an openai chat call to redwood with node snippet. (shares snippet) you see we change client.init('redwood') and call client.generate(...). the rest is very similar.
06:12 Marcus Lee: nice, how about rate limits and quotas? we run bursts of 200 qps for short windows.
06:18 Sofia Liu: for hosted we have tiered rate limits but can provide burst allowances; for Dedicated you get guaranteed throughput. Dedicated is typically for steady high QPS and predictable p99. we can model your QPS in the benchmark.
06:35 Dana Ortiz: what's typical effort for migration? small services vs entire platform?
06:40 Jordan Park: many customers do incremental migration - start with a noncritical route or a pilot. timeline for a pilot is usually 2-4 weeks including benchmarks, config, and a small canary. larger migrations depend on integration depth.
06:53 Aisha Khan: compliance - do you support audit trails we can ingest into our SIEM?
06:58 Sofia Liu: yes, audit logs are available and can be shipped to customer S3/kinesis or integrated via our audit API.
07:08 Jordan Park: ok we'll open the parity mapping spreadsheet now - you'll see a column for openai param, anthopic param, together param, and redwood equivalent, plus notes about behavioral diffs.
07:22 Marcus Lee: that doc will be really helpful. does it also include example payloads for streaming and function call?
07:28 Sofia Liu: yes, and SDK snippets for node/python and a migration checklist. we'll attach the doc after the call.
07:36 Aisha Khan: for benchmarks, we care about p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens.
07:42 Sofia Liu: understood. we'll run a perf test with your payloads and measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens consumed, and then produce cost estimates for hosted and a rough for Dedicated.
07:54 Marcus Lee: any gotchas with token counting differences across models?
07:58 Sofia Liu: yes some tokenizers differ; the parity doc flags approximate token delta and we'll report tokens observed during tests.
08:06 Dana Ortiz: what about streaming reliability? sometimes partial events drop or reorder.
08:11 Sofia Liu: we have retries on the streaming layer and sequence ids to reassemble; we'll show logs in the console tracing. occasionally noise in transcription can make things seem off but the payloads are stable.
08:26 Jordan Park: let's talk pilot scope: suggested pilot = 2 routes, one chat agent for internal support and one embedding rerank for search, run for 2 weeks, measure p99 and cost, then decide on next. does that align?
08:40 Aisha Khan: yes that sounds reasonable. timeline-wise we want to finish a pilot before end of July.
08:46 Jordan Park: great, so next steps: a) jordan shares parity mapping and sdk snippets by 6/20, b) aisha sends three representative payload sets by 6/19, c) sofia runs perf tests and shares results by 6/22, d) security scoping call targeted week of 6/23.
09:05 Marcus Lee: one last question - do you support on-prem GPU quantized runtimes? we have regulatory customers that need on-prem.
09:12 Sofia Liu: yes, our private deployment supports on-prem runtime and we supply quantization recommendations; some kernels vary by hardware so we do a short onboarding to pick optimal quantization and kernel.
09:26 Aisha Khan: ok thanks, this was helpful. we'll wait for the parity doc and send payloads.
09:32 Jordan Park: awesome, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with an email with artifacts and calendar invites for the security scoping and the perf run.
09:40 (call ends)
